content:
incident-bot: Paging oncall (P1) — elevated 5xx for public API via us-east-1a IPv6 paths. Trigger: 30m rolling error spike > 15%. Auto-runbook: check routing, LB dual-stack, and PMTUD failures. @maria (oncall) paged. :rotating_light:

maria: ACKed. seeing 502/504 mostly on backend egress to transit peer over IPv6. IPv4 looks fine.

jordan: confirm — cloud status for us-east-1a shows no platform-wide EC2 outage. Could be MTU/DF path issue. Any recent config changes?

maria: no config changes on our side. Quick packet captures from router show ICMPv6 'Packet too big' responses but they aren't reaching client side (PMTUD blackhole).

nate: pushing logs — truncated pcap snippet:

```
17:23:45.123 IP6 fe80::a -> 2001:db8::1: UDP, length 1500
17:23:45.124 IP6 2001:db8::1 -> fe80::a: ICMP6, Packet too big, mtu=1280
17:23:45.125 IP6 fe80::a -> 2001:db8::1: UDP, length 1500
# but subsequent ICMPs not seen by client side
```

irene: That MTU (1280) rings a bell — our transit peer sometimes enforces 1280 for IPv6 when jumbo frames are mis-advertised. If ICMPs are filtered by a provider firewall, PMTUD fails.

kevin: Customers impacted: A handful of enterprise tenants in us-east-1 with IPv6-preferred stacks. Support reports increased error rates for streaming and websocket connections. support-bot will create a customer ticket bundle.

support-bot: Created CS tickets: T-2410, T-2411, T-2412. Notifying account teams.

maria: Immediate mitigation options:
- enable IPv4-only VIPs for affected routes (fast)
- force TCP MSS clamping on our NAT/GW to 1280
- push kernel tcp tweaks to fallback clients (harder)

jordan: Let's do IPv4-only VIPs as 1st step and enable MSS clamp at the edge. MSS clamp command on our egress boxes:

```
# on linux edge
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
# for nftables setups
nft add rule inet mangle postrouting tcp flags syn tcp option maxseg size set 1220
```

maria: rolling MSS-clamp to all egress nodes in us-east-1a now, starting with small batch. Also creating IPv4-only ALB listeners for the problematic service (will preserve sessions).

nate: MSS clamp applied to 3/20 egress nodes — observed drop in 5xx on those nodes (from 18% -> 4%).

irene: Nice. Are we sure there isn't a broken provider firewall silently dropping ICMPv6? We should open a ticket with the transit provider.

maria: opening provider ticket, linking pcap and traceroutes.

maria: traceroute6 shows first broken hop at provider edge, they responded with 'we're investigating' (ticket P-3884).

jordan: Customer-level mitigation: for each affected tenant, route traffic via dual-region failover (us-east-1b) where IPv6 path healthy. But that's heavier — prefer MSS and IPv4-only VIPs for minimal disruption.

kevin: Communicating to affected customers: Initial note sent — summary, mitigation, ETA ~2 hours for full rollout. We'll follow up with RCA when done.

maria: Handoff incoming: @jordan taking oncall at 18:00 UTC. Current status: MSS clamp rolled to 20/20 nodes in us-east-1a; IPv4-only ALB listeners active for service-prod. Error rate decreased cluster-wide to ~2-3%. Provider ticket still open.

jordan: ACK takeover. I will keep monitoring for regressions and coordinate provider escalations. Any request for infra changes?

maria: No further changes expected. Please keep support looped and update incident timeline.

jordan: Noted. Also adding temporary instrumentation: tag all IPv6 requests in logs with "ipv6-mtu-2025-03" for postmortem queries.

nate: Side note — one lib we use sets IPv6 preferencing for dual-stack clients. We should add a client-side fallback to IPv4 earlier in our SDKs. Filing tech debt: DEBT-1283.

irene: Good call. Also include an egress policy to allow ICMPv6 type 2 (Packet Too Big) through provider ACLs as a follow-up.

jordan: Do we have a tentative severity and customer impact summary for the postmortem?

maria: Severity P1 (service degradation for subset of tenants). Impact: ~12 enterprise customers experienced errors, some timed-out SDKs; no data loss. Mitigations: MSS clamp + IPv4 listeners + routing fallback. Planned follow-ups: provider ACL fix, SDK fallback, long-term: prefer-path detection and active PMTUD probes.

support-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-1742001234-ipv6-mtu. Postmortem task card ID: PM-6789.

jordan: Closing loop — provider confirmed they were silently dropping ICMPv6 when jumbo MTU was negotiated upstream. They applied an ACL change and tests show ICMPv6 now traverses. We'll keep MSS clamp for 24h as safety then remove.

kevin: Customer update draft: short summary + actions + mitigation + ETA for RCA. Please review: "We experienced elevated errors for IPv6 traffic in us-east-1a due to PMTUD failures between our edge and a transit peer. We mitigated by temporarily falling back to IPv4 and applying MSS clamping; provider applied ACL changes. Root cause analysis and next steps will follow." :thumbsup:

maria: LGTM. Marking incident as mitigated. Will start writeup.

jordan: Incident status -> mitigated. Assigning action items:
- Provider confirmation & closure (jordan)
- SDK fallback implementation (nate)
- Postmortem writeup (maria)
- Infra: allow icmpv6/PTB through egress ACLs and remove long-term MSS clamp after 24h (kevin)

maria: thanks all. will fill in timeline and metrics in postmortem. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
